# MaiWoL

> Wake-on-LAN and remote power management app for Android. Sends Magic Packets over LAN or WAN/DDNS, checks device status via ICMP and port probing, and can trigger remote shutdown via SSH or webhooks. Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, GPL-3.0, no ads or trackers.

MaiWoL wakes devices with UDP Magic Packets (with optional SecureOn password),
verifies whether they came online through ICMP ping and common service-port
checks (SMB 445, RPC 135, NetBIOS 139, RDP 3389, WSD 5357, SSH 22), and can
send them back to sleep or shut down via SSH commands or HTTP webhooks.

## Core features

- Wake-on-LAN: local broadcast or WAN/DDNS unicast, 1–20 packet bursts, SecureOn support
- Remote shutdown/sleep: SSH command execution or HTTP GET/POST webhooks
- Status polling: ICMP ping plus multi-port service checks, tri-state (online/standby/unreachable)
- Rootless MAC discovery via the Shizuku API (works around Android 10+ /proc/net/arp restrictions)
- Device grouping, batch wake, home-screen widgets, and a Quick Settings tile
- Scheduling via AlarmManager (RTC_WAKEUP) with boot-persistence
- Encrypted (AES-256-GCM) local backup/restore of device lists
- PIN/biometric app lock

## Automation (Tasker / MacroDroid / ADB)

- Broadcast action: `com.mai.wol.ACTION_WAKE_DEVICE`
- Target package: `com.mai.wol`
- Extras: `device_name` (String), `device_id` (Long/Int), `mac_address` (String),
  `ip_address` (String), `local_ip` (String), `port` (Int), `packet_count` (Int),
  `secure_on` (String)
- Example: `adb shell am broadcast -a com.mai.wol.ACTION_WAKE_DEVICE -p com.mai.wol --es device_name "Workstation"`
